text: Mid-course test, track one. Dr Eka is here today to talk about how we can use drones to help with the problems created by global warming. Yes, thank you for inviting me, Professor. So, I think everybody here knows what a drone is. It's basically a flying computer, a bit like a small plane, controlled from the ground. We can use drones in many different ways. For example, we can send drones into different locations to collect information about the weather. They help us to find out about how climates change over time. For example, how humid or dry they become. And I believe you said that we can also use drones to plant trees. Yes! As you know, we are cutting down trees in rainforests all over the world. We're trying to plant new trees at the same time, but the problem is that we cut down about 15 billion trees a year, but only plant 9 billion. However, by using drones we can now plant trees from the air. The drones fly 3 meters above the ground and are able to plant 120 trees per minute. It's actually possible to plant as many as 100,000 trees in one day. That's amazing! In my opinion, one of the best ways that we use drones is for going into dangerous places, such as areas where there are forest fires or floods. Drones can help us to find and save wildlife that is in danger. So, are there any disadvantages to drone technology? For example, is it very expensive? Well, drones are like computers. You can get cheap ones and you can get very expensive ones. Our department at the university bought a drone last year for about 1,500 euros. I tested more expensive ones and I personally feel that our drone is just as good. It's quite easy to use. We control it using an app from a mobile phone. It can fly for 45 minutes at up to 40 kilometers per hour. The problem with this kind of drone is that it uses batteries, and obviously you have to charge them after flying, which can take up quite a lot of time. It's a good drone for flying. It's a good drone for flying. It's a good drone for flying.
